name: Digital Decade Policy Programme Decision
impact_assessment: None (staff working document instead of an IA)
evidence_rating: monitoring only: annual Commission KPI tracking against 2030 targets; no assessment of whether the governance mechanism itself changed outcomes
summary: The Digital Decade programme sets EU targets for 2030 on connectivity, skills, business digitalisation and public services, and makes the Commission report progress every year. Its own reports show basic 5G at 96.8% of households and online public services above 80%, but the EU is far off target on AI use by firms (about 20% vs 75%), basic digital skills (just over 60% vs 80%), fibre and chips. No study has assessed whether the programme's governance changed what Member States do.

indicators.objective: No impact assessment (the Commission judged one unnecessary and issued a staff working document instead) and no LFS indicators. The Decision itself sets the 2030 digital targets (Article 4) with KPIs tracked in the annual State of the Digital Decade report

indicators.indicator: Gigabit coverage for all households; 5G in all populated areas
indicators.evidence: Basic 5G covers 96.8% of households (2026); fibre-to-the-premises 69% and very-high-capacity networks 82% (2025 report) - FTTP 'not enough to reach 100% by 2030'; stand-alone 5G lagging.

indicators.indicator: 75% of enterprises using cloud, big data or AI
indicators.evidence: 2026: 46.7% of firms use cloud, 39.9% data analytics, nearly 20% AI; AI, cloud and data analytics progress rated 'deeply unsatisfactory' in 2025.

indicators.indicator: 80% of adults with basic digital skills; 20 million ICT specialists
indicators.evidence: More than 60% have at least basic skills (2026); ICT specialist shortages and gender gap persist; both rated deeply unsatisfactory in 2025.

indicators.indicator: EU share of global semiconductor production
indicators.evidence: About 10% of the global market at the programme's launch; secondary summaries of the 2026 report put it at 9%, far below target; the Commission says semiconductors still lag.
82% for citizens and 86% for businesses (2025 report).

indicators.indicator: National roadmaps and follow-up of recommendations
indicators.evidence: All Member States adopted roadmaps: 1,910 measures worth EUR 288.6bn (EUR 205.1bn public, 1.14% of EU GDP); 57% of 306 country recommendations from 2024 addressed, mostly only partly (12% significant changes).

literature.citation: European Commission (2025), State of the Digital Decade 2025: Keep building the EU's sovereignty and digital future, COM(2025) 290
literature.title: State of the Digital Decade 2025: Keep building the EU's sovereignty and digital future
literature.outcomes: connectivity; skills; business digitalisation; public services
literature.headline: Uneven progress: edge nodes, e-health and basic 5G near targets; AI, cloud, data analytics, ICT specialists and basic skills 'deeply unsatisfactory'; FTTP 69%, VHCN 82%; national roadmaps worth EUR 288.6bn; 57% of 2024 recommendations addressed
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's own scorecard shows the EU on track for basic 5G and online services but far off its 2030 goals for AI use by firms, digital skills, fibre and chips.

literature.citation: European Commission (2026), State of the Digital Decade 2026 report (news summary), Commission news, 17 June 2026
literature.title: State of the Digital Decade 2026 report (news summary)
literature.headline: 96.8% of households have basic 5G; fibre, semiconductors and computing capacity lag; more than 60% have basic digital skills; ICT specialist shortages persist; targets to be reviewed in 2027
literature.summary_plain: The 2026 scorecard shows more progress on mobile coverage and skills, but fibre, chips and business use of advanced technology still trail the 2030 goals; the targets will be reviewed in 2027.

literature.title: EUrope's digital transition: Assessing the effectiveness of the 2030 Digital Decade Policy Programme
literature.venue: REGROUP Focus Paper No. 2 (European Policy Centre; republished by CIDOB)
literature.method: desk review of the 2023 and 2024 State of the Digital Decade reports and national roadmaps, with country cases (Finland, Belgium, Italy, Bulgaria) and expert discussions
literature.outcomes: progress towards Digital Decade targets (skills, connectivity, business digitalisation, public services), funding, coherence
literature.headline: Drawing on the Commission's own projections, the EU is off track on all Digital Decade targets: only 59% of people are projected to have basic digital skills by 2030 against an 80% target, and about 12 million ICT specialists against a 20 million goal.
literature.summary_plain: A Brussels think tank reviewed how the EU is doing against its 2030 digital goals. Using official progress reports, it concludes Europe is behind on every target and calls for more realistic goals, better funding and stronger accountability.
literature.quality: Secondary analysis of Commission monitoring data plus expert discussions; no new data or causal design.
literature.interested_party: Funded under the EU's Horizon Europe programme (REGROUP project)
literature.citation: Giulia Torchio (2025), EUrope's digital transition: Assessing the effectiveness of the 2030 Digital Decade Policy Programme, REGROUP Focus Paper No. 2 (European Policy Centre; republished by CIDOB)
